definitions: A type of aldol reaction in organic chemistry that creates new carbon-carbon bonds with high stereoselectivity, leading to the formation of chiral products.
A chemical reaction that forms β-hydroxy carbonyl compounds or β-hydroxy imine derivatives with control over the absolute or relative stereochemistry of the newly formed chiral centers.
examples: The asymmetric aldol reaction is a powerful tool in synthetic organic chemistry.
Many natural products are synthesized using an asymmetric aldol reaction as a key step.
Catalysts are crucial for achieving high enantioselectivity in an asymmetric aldol reaction.
